newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Ciech eyes Q1 IPO of PLN 200-400 mln.
newsitem.headline: Polish Ciech eyes Q1 IPO of PLN 200-400 mln.

text.p: Poland's largest chemicals trader Ciech SA plans an initial public offering in the first quarter of next year worth between 200 million and 400 million zlotys, the firm's president said on Wednesday.

"The offer could be from 200 million zlotys to 400 million zlotys but it can't be ruled out that it will be more," Zdzislaw Matkiewicz told a news conference, adding that the state treasury currently held 51 percent of Ciech.
The remaining 49 percent belongs to numerous, mostly state-owned companies in the chemical sector.

Matkiewicz said the ex-rights new issue should take place in the first quarter of 1997 and a bourse entry in the second, but that more precise details would be available after an extraordinary shareholders meeting on December 12.
He said that in the future he envisioned the state's ownership dropping to between five and 10 percent.
Ciech board member Krzysztof Staniszewski told Reuters that it was not yet clear if the state would sell shares on the Warsaw bourse after the issue to reduce its stake.

Matkiewicz said the firm did not need a strategic investor but that privatisation advisers -- state-owned Bank Pekao SA and NM Rothschild and Sons Ltd -- were seeking a possible international financial investor.
Staniszewski said there would be three or four tranches for large, medium and small investors and employees.
Matkiewicz said the large-investor tranche could account for 30 to 40 percent of the issue.
Board Chairman Jerzy Reszka said the firm wanted to buy firms in the pharmaceutical sector, its most profitable sector.
Matkiewicz said 1996 earnings could prove slightly worse than in 1995 but would not give figures.
Ciech netted 50 million zlotys in 1995 and 48 million in 1994 on sales of about 2.7 billion zlotys and 3.6 billion zlotys respectively.
Matkiewicz said shareholders would also vote to give the firm the right to issue convertible bonds but that details would not be set.
